title: Port Of Alaska
specs: Handles 5.5 million tons of fuel and freight annually
Located on upper Cook Inlet with highest tides in the United States, tide range almost 40 feet
Modernization Program underway to replace aging docks and improve safety and efficiency
All visitors must show a government-issued photo ID at the port security gate
Firearms, ammunition, fireworks, and other explosive devices are prohibited inside the port security perimeter
gap: No visitor or tour services described
blurb: Don Young Port of Alaska handles over 5.5 million tons of fuel and freight annually, including containers, liquid bulk, dry bulk, break bulk, and cruise ships. It serves as Alaska's primary inbound-cargo port, handling about half of all Alaska inbound freight. The port features extensive infrastructure including cargo yards, fuel storage, cranes, and a skilled workforce, located on upper Cook Inlet near major transportation systems.
extraNote: All vehicles are subject to random security screening · Third-floor conference room in the Don Young Port of Alaska administrative office at 1871 Anchorage Port Road
